verdict.tagline: Endless procedural depths hide frustrating controls and archaic design choices.
for_you_if: you love randomized dungeon runs filled with weird items
you enjoy mastering challenging rogue-like action
not_for_you_if: you need custom keyboard or gamepad support
you rely on in-game guides to understand items
you cannot commit to continuous single sessions

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial reviewers struggle with hard input barriers while established players focus on deep randomized content.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Explorers discover randomized rooms and an assortment of items.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game featuring randomly-generated rooms and an assortment of items and achievements.

citations.review_text: This game is a classic for a reason. The mix of intuitive gameplay, challeging enemies, randomly-generated rooms, hundreds of items and the sheer scale of the achievements makes for a game with an almost unlimited amount of playtime and replayability. Highly recommend to anyone who likes grinding for hours to improve skill and to unlock new items. 10/10.

A tiny game about a crying kid in a basement somehow became one of the most addictive roguelikes ever made. The Flash version is rough around the edges, but that only makes it more charming.
The runs are chaotic, the items are weird, and every chest feels like a gamble. One minute you're a god with a broken build, the next you're getting destroyed by a random enemy and questioning your life choices.
The game is unfair, weird, and full of surprises — exactly why people keep coming back.
9/10 – A legendary classic. Small game, huge addiction.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the original version runs on the Flash engine, which causes performance issues, lag on modern hardware, and limited full-screen display options that stretch the borders.

citations.review_text:
[b]This game honestly feels way harder than its sequel.[/b]
And no, it's just not because the Flash version runs like a fcn slideshow and you have to play it in a small window. Some rooms and enemies just feel unbalanced, especially the eternal ones.

But what I especially like is that some items (like Ouija board), secret and arcade rooms feel much more valuable, and you actually wanna find and use them. Every item feels viable and useful. Absolutely love it.

I'm glad this game became the start point for the best roguelike game ever, and if you've already got Dead God in Rebirth, I'd definitely recommend giving this game a try to test your mechanical skills

I wouldn't actively recommend Flash Isaac, but there are no neutral options & it's a lot more positive than negative to me.

As someone with over three thousands hours and 100% completion on its remake, TBOI:Rebirth, TBOI is a fine game. It functions properly, and overall it isn't too unfamiliar coming from the remake. The game is enjoyably balanced for the most part, and has very good Flash era graphics that I personally prefer over the pixel art art direction TBOI:R takes.

My main grip with this game is that a lot of rooms are seriously unfair. I'm not even talking about Eternal Edition (I'll get to it), just straight up normal rooms have layouts and enemies you literally can't do anything about unless you have flight, spectral or any sort of quick way to kill enemies and/or escape. And with how scarce dps upgrades are, it can get especially infuriating. The hitless achievements are looking horrific, and I think I might need to reset until I get a stupid op first two floors and then somehow not fumble later on. Which isn't a good look.

Eternal Edition has its own set of issues, eternal enemies are not very well thought through and often lead to unfair situations. However, I have found Eternal's hard mode to be significantly easier than playing on normal mode or simply on Wrath of the Lamb. You get a lot of HP upgrades, and typically getting one damage upgrade will be enough to finish a run, as the final bosses are ridiculously easier. It's a weird balance. TBOI is very strange in that regard, sometimes extremely good sometimes horridly bad.

Overall, I would recommend TBOI:R over TBOI, as the remake does right everything that Flash did wrong. I will not talk about my issues with Rebirth here I have a completely other review for that. If you come from Rebirth and are curious at how Flash plays, I'd say it'd be right up your alley. It's more Isaac afterall, who wouldn't want more Isaac? cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term veterans embrace external wikis and unbroken session lengths despite encountering progress-blocking bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks in-game item explanations, making external wiki use essential to understand what items do.

citations.review_text: Great flash game! Definitely worth getting if you like arcade style shooters. No save options for continuing runs which means you must devote some real time while playing. Very fun and having everything randomly generate makes it never become boring with every run being unique. Very little in game item explenations so using the wiki to figure out what things actually do is essential. Will require skill and memorization to become good but there is heavy RNG in this game which is unavoidable at times. Still worth every minute of playing.

I would recommend this game with reservations. Firstly, it is significantly harder than Rebirth/Repentance. Do not expect to get wins easily if you find Repentance easy. Resources are also much scarcer so it's not uncommon to have runs where you cannot enter each treasure room etc. Be picky about using your keys and bombs. But do not be picky about HP pickups; you can hold a HUGE amount of containers and soul hearts. 

Many of the mechanics from Repentance do work in this game such as secret room locations, Devil/Angel room spawn rules etc. The Wrath of the Lamb wiki isn't nearly as good as the Repentance wiki but it does have a lot of helpful information so do not hesitate to check it for help. Finally, hard mode honestly sucks. It's not well balanced. The hard mode achievements will be by far the most difficult to achieve if you want to 100%.

The biggest legacy of Edmund McMillen, a true classic flash game.
Altough it is universally agreed that Rebirth and all its DLCs are better than the classic game, this is where it all started: the bosses, the characters, the bullet hell, the entire concept of Isaac, it's all in this single game, all in its buggy and unfair glory.
The only thing I miss after playing Rebirth first are the synergies; those combinations of items that could entirelly break the game balance, making you insta-kill bosses and basically getting you a guaranteed win. In the classic one, luck is still a thing, but you won't be getting any better by getting Brimstone (which definitively was buffed before going to Rebirth). You'll still need to get good.
Also, one thing that really got on my nerves that was only a thing in this one were the ETERNAL monsters (the ones that look like Delirium minions) that came with Hardmode; in short, take an enemy and make it unfair to the MAX, forcing you to completely ignore every other enemy and focus entirelly on it. AND THEY SPAWN AT LEAST ONE IN ALMOST EVERY ROOM YOU ENTER! And the bosses are not safe either! They will tear you apart if you're not dodging everything they throw at you (also, Mom and Mom's Heart/It Lives are guaranteed to be Eternal). At least the bosses give you a eternal heart for beating them, so skill is rewarded. In Rebirth, all of these abominations were fused into Delirium, so no more suffering from exploring extra rooms.

Now, for the achievements:
Other than a few extra challenges, it boils down to grinding the first 10 Mom's Heart kills, killing every boss with every character on Hardmode (just like in Rebirth) and doing all challenges.
However, one should be wary of the No-Hit achievements, especially the Dark Boy and Mama's Boy. You can use the challenges to beat all of them, but I recommend doing that for Basement and Caves, then using Isaac and his D6 to get the rest. Trust me, you'll suffer less this way.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs that can trap players inside eternal trap rooms.

citations.review_text:
Eternal mode is absolute bs. Sure you get eternal hearts on every floor, but it does not change the fact that some eternal enemies and bosses are just too much to handle. You can also find eternal trap rooms, which can give you some nice angel room items, but these rooms are NOT guaranteed. You can also get stuck in those rooms, because of a stupid bug. Cathedral and the Chest are insanely hard in eternal mode as well, because quite often  you will have to go against multiple eternal bosses in the same room.

On top of everything i have listed, item pool in the game is atrocious. Most of the space bar items are useless and many passive items are as well. Overall, i am just tired of this game. It can be fun, when you have that 1 in a thousand great run, but most of the times it is torture.

Time to get to rebirth now, thankfully it is MUCH better
